newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index loses ground on VUB bank fall.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index loses ground on VUB bank fall.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with losses to shares of bank VUB pulling the SAX index down 4.51 points to 204.40.
VUB fell 110 crowns to 1,720 and steel maker VSZ eased 32 crowns to 600, though both saw only minor volumes change hands.

Brokers said the market mired in a general downtrend, with no end currently in sight. "Investors and shareholders are very cautious at the moment as it is risky to operate on the falling market," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
"The decline may last for just a while, but it also might remain until the usual new year's rise," he added.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta was the most active issue on the day with 400 shares trading, closing up 20 crowns at 2,020, but with a 0.64 percent lower average price.
"If we take this small volume into account, nothing serious had happened in Nafta," Sykora said.
Dealers said the market is anxiously waiting the firm's shareholders' meeting next week as its new owners are expected to reveal their plans for the firm.
Overall volume fell to 77,713 shares from 875,221 on Monday, while turnover decreased to 35.03 million crowns, from 374.69 million.
